idiom_name: Vapor route closure returning a ResponseEncodable value
implementation_notes: Vapor registers one closure per route (app.get("users", ":id") { req in ... }) and that closure is the Action; the Responder role is the returned value, because anything ResponseEncodable - a Content struct encoded as JSON, a String, or an explicit Response with status, headers and body - becomes the HTTP response, and thrown Abort errors are mapped to status codes. The domain must be a plain service type injected into the route collection, never the Request. An explicit responder type is justified when one action must serve several formats (an Accept-driven switch returning Response or Content); otherwise returning a Content struct is the idiomatic responder.
pitfalls: Route handlers must be Sendable in current Vapor versions; capturing non-Sendable state in the closure is a compile error or a data race.
Throwing Abort is the supported error-to-response path: returning nil or an empty body for a missing resource yields a 200.
Blocking work (synchronous file or database access) inside the async closure blocks an EventLoop thread and stalls other connections.
